actor: Agent hook execution security engineer, Anthropic Claude Code
job: Reworking how repository-supplied session-start hooks and settings files are loaded, so opening a cloned folder no longer executes them on the trust decision alone.
outcome: A shipped default where a repository's session-start hook stays inert until approved in a step separate from trusting the workspace.
motivation: The hook lands on a workstation holding live credentials, not in a throwaway build container, and no install-time defence ever sees it.

task.who: Claude Code settings loading and hook execution engineers
task.what: Hold repository-supplied hooks inert until separately approved
task.where: Claude Code settings resolution and hook dispatch path
task.why: Workspace trust was never a decision about hooks
task.how: Per-entry approval recorded in user-scope settings, keyed by digest

actor: Workspace Trust maintainer, Microsoft Visual Studio Code
job: Owning the trust prompt and the tasks that run on folder open, deciding whether trust alone stays sufficient to start a repository's own commands.
outcome: A default build where a repository's folder-open task is listed and confirmed, or held inert, rather than started by the trust click.
motivation: The one control in front of this path is a dialogue the product trained everyone to dismiss in order to start working.

task.who: Visual Studio Code workspace trust and task system maintainers
task.what: Gate folder-open tasks behind a confirmation of their own
task.where: Workspace trust subsystem and task runner in Insiders builds
task.why: Trust answers a different question than auto-run does
task.how: Itemised run list in the trust flow, entries inert by default

motivation: A behaviour change nobody documents reaches nobody, and the milestone is also what stops the work slipping behind larger features.

task.what: Book the auto-run gate into a shipping milestone
